cards.text: We're at the end of Ecclesiastes, and the book steps back to talk about the Teacher, the son of David and king in Jerusalem (Ecclesiastes 1:1). It's like the little "about the author" blurb on the back of a cookbook, and the first thing it says is that he was wise.

cards.question: The Teacher was wise, but he kept all that wisdom to himself.

cards.text: And this man put in the WORK: he pondered, searched out and arranged many proverbs. Friend, it takes me THREE tries just to line up one shelf of cookie boxes.

cards.question: The Teacher searched to find delightful sayings. What did he want the words he recorded to be?

cards.text: Next, the book paints a picture: the words of the wise are like goads. Friend, I'm a stamper, so pictures are the ONLY thing I do, and I am LEANING in.

cards.question: After the words of the wise are compared to goads, the anthologies of the masters get a picture too. What are they like?
The anthologies of the masters are pictured as nails. How are those nails set?

cards.text: And who drives those nails in? The book says a single Shepherd.
Then the book speaks to "my son" and gives him one more warning, this one about books and study. Anytime somebody gives me one more warning, I sit up straight like the oven timer just went off.

cards.question: The warning to "my son" says there is no end to the making of many books.
The warning goes on: much study ___ the body.

cards.text: Now, when all has been heard, the book gives the conclusion of the matter: fear God and keep His commandments. No fine print, friend, and trust me, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer full of warranty cards, so I know fine print.

cards.question: Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the ___ duty of man.

cards.text: And the very last line of the whole book gives the reason: God will bring every deed into judgment. That's how the Teacher signs off, friend.

cards.question: God's judgment reaches the hidden things too. Which of them does it bring in?

answers.text: The good and the evil ones
